I’m treating this as an external feasibility audit of the exported schedule, not a review of the producer’s model. I’ll re-derive the public constraints from [`/app/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md`](/app/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md), inspect the data and exported rows, then run independent checks family by family with event-sweep validation on the intervals.

The export is degenerate: 42 `case` rows, every case unscheduled, and no `tray`, `cart`, or `batch` rows at all. I’m pulling the public data now to determine whether that still violates mandatory coverage, scenario recourse, or other public requirements.

I’ve confirmed there are no interval rows in the submission, so the interval-based families will mostly reduce to “no witness rows to validate.” I’m now checking whether the all-deferred plan is already falsified by public coverage rules, starting with mandatory-case requirements and any feasible public lower bound on served cases.

The remaining question is whether the all-deferred export can still satisfy the public “mandatory only as last resort” rule. I’m running an independent feasibility search for single mandatory cases using only public room, inventory, route, and scenario data so I can distinguish “bad objective” from an actual public-rule violation.
